$schema: text uses [[answer]] to mark a blank. Multiple blanks per item are answered in order.

items.title: etcd snapshot save
items.text:
ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl \
  --endpoints=https://127.0.0.1:[[2379]] \
  --[[cacert]]=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/ca.crt \
  --[[cert]]=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/server.crt \
  --[[key]]=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/server.key \
  snapshot [[save]] /opt/etcd-backup.db
items.why: etcd speaks mutual TLS only — all three certificate flags are mandatory, and 2379 is the client port (2380 is peer).

items.title: etcd restore, then the two edits
items.text:
etcdctl snapshot [[restore]] /opt/etcd-backup.db --[[data-dir]]=/var/lib/etcd-restore

# then in /etc/kubernetes/manifests/[[etcd.yaml]] change BOTH:
#   the container's --data-dir flag
#   the [[hostPath]].path of the etcd-data volume
items.why: --data-dir is the path inside the container; the hostPath volume maps it to the host. Change only one and the restore serves stale data.

items.title: kubeadm upgrade, control-plane node
items.text:
kubectl drain cp-1 --[[ignore-daemonsets]]
sudo apt-mark [[unhold]] kubeadm
sudo apt-get install -y kubeadm=1.35.0-1.1
sudo apt-mark [[hold]] kubeadm
sudo kubeadm upgrade [[plan]]
sudo kubeadm upgrade [[apply]] v1.35.0
sudo systemctl [[daemon-reload]] && sudo systemctl restart [[kubelet]]
kubectl [[uncordon]] cp-1
items.why: 'apply' runs on the first control-plane node only; every other node uses 'upgrade node'. kubeadm never upgrades the kubelet package, so that restart is yours to do.

items.title: kubeadm upgrade, worker node
items.text:
kubectl drain worker-1 --ignore-daemonsets --[[delete-emptydir-data]]
# on worker-1:
sudo kubeadm upgrade [[node]]
sudo apt-mark unhold kubelet kubectl && sudo apt-get install -y kubelet=1.35.0-1.1 kubectl=1.35.0-1.1
sudo systemctl daemon-reload && sudo systemctl restart kubelet
kubectl uncordon worker-1
items.why: Workers only refresh their local config, so it is 'upgrade node', never 'upgrade apply'.

items.title: Role and RoleBinding, imperative
items.text:
kubectl create role pod-reader --[[verb]]=get,list,watch --[[resource]]=pods -n dev
kubectl create rolebinding read-pods --[[role]]=pod-reader --[[serviceaccount]]=dev:app-sa -n dev
kubectl auth [[can-i]] list pods -n dev --[[as]]=system:serviceaccount:dev:app-sa
items.why: --serviceaccount takes namespace:name. The auth check asks the API server's own authorizer, so a 'yes' is proof.

items.title: ClusterRole limited to one named object
items.text:
kubectl create role cm-editor --verb=get,update --resource=configmaps \
  --[[resource-name]]=app-config -n dev
kubectl create role log-reader --verb=get --resource=[[pods/log]] -n dev
items.why: --resource-name narrows a rule to one object; pods/log is a distinct sub-resource, so granting 'pods' does not grant kubectl logs.

items.title: HA control plane join
items.text:
sudo kubeadm init --[[control-plane-endpoint]] "k8s-api.example.com:6443" --[[upload-certs]]

sudo kubeadm join k8s-api.example.com:6443 --token <t> \
  --discovery-token-ca-cert-hash sha256:<hash> \
  --[[control-plane]] --[[certificate-key]] <key>
items.why: --control-plane-endpoint is baked into every kubeconfig and cert SAN at init time; the kubeadm-certs Secret created by --upload-certs expires after two hours.

items.title: Fresh join command
items.text: kubeadm [[token]] create --[[print-join-command]]
items.why: Join tokens expire after 24h by default, so the one printed at install time is usually dead.

items.title: Helm install with values
items.text:
helm repo add ingress-nginx <url> && helm repo [[update]]
helm [[show]] values ingress-nginx/ingress-nginx > /tmp/values.yaml
helm install ing ingress-nginx/ingress-nginx -n ingress --[[create-namespace]] \
  --[[version]] 4.11.0 -f /tmp/values.yaml
helm [[list]] -A
items.why: Without --version Helm silently installs the newest chart; 'show values' is how you learn the key paths you are allowed to --set.

items.title: Kustomize overlay
items.text:
kubectl [[kustomize]] ./overlays/prod        # render to stdout first
kubectl apply [[-k]] ./overlays/prod
items.why: -k runs the kustomize build; apply -f on kustomization.yaml tries to apply the file as an object and fails.

items.title: Discover a custom resource offline
items.text:
kubectl [[get]] crds
kubectl [[api-resources]] --api-group=cert-manager.io
kubectl [[explain]] certificate --[[recursive]] | head -40
items.why: api-resources gives the plural name, short name and scope; explain --recursive gives the whole schema from the connected API server — always the right version.

items.title: Logs of the container that died
items.text:
kubectl logs web-7d9 -n prod --[[previous]]
kubectl logs web-7d9 -n prod --[[all-containers]] --tail=50
kubectl describe pod web-7d9 -n prod | grep -A3 '[[Last State]]'
items.why: The running container is a fresh restart with no history; --previous reads the instance that crashed, and Last State carries its exit code.

items.title: Events, newest last
items.text: kubectl get events -A --[[sort-by]]=.[[lastTimestamp]] | tail -20
items.why: The control plane narrates every scheduling refusal, pull failure, probe failure and OOM kill into Events with a reason string.

items.title: When kubectl is dead
items.text:
ls /etc/kubernetes/[[manifests]]/
sudo [[crictl]] ps -a --name kube-apiserver
sudo crictl [[logs]] <container-id> 2>&1 | tail -30
sudo [[journalctl]] -u kubelet --no-pager -n 50
items.why: Control-plane components are static Pods run by the kubelet straight from disk, so they can be inspected and repaired with no API server.

items.title: Static Pod path
items.text: grep [[staticPodPath]] /var/lib/kubelet/[[config.yaml]]
items.why: That kubelet config field is what makes /etc/kubernetes/manifests special; on an unfamiliar cluster, confirm rather than assume.

items.title: Node conditions
items.text:
kubectl describe node worker-1 | sed -n '/[[Conditions]]/,/Addresses/p'
systemctl [[status]] kubelet
kubeadm certs [[check-expiration]]
items.why: Conditions is the kubelet's own report card, and Ready=False carries a message naming the cause. Cluster-wide NotReady with cert errors points at expiry.

items.title: Service selects nothing
items.text:
kubectl get svc,[[endpoints]] web -n prod
kubectl get pods -n prod --[[show-labels]]
items.why: An empty ENDPOINTS column proves the fault is label selection or readiness, not routing — which collapses the search space immediately.

items.title: In-cluster probe Pod
items.text:
kubectl run probe --image=busybox:1.36 --rm -it --restart=[[Never]] -- \
  sh -c 'nslookup web.prod.svc.[[cluster.local]]; wget -qO- --timeout=2 web.prod:80'
items.why: --restart=Never makes it a bare Pod rather than a Deployment; testing from inside the cluster network is the only place a ClusterIP exists.

items.title: Force-delete a stuck Pod
items.text:
kubectl get pod web -o jsonpath='{.metadata.[[finalizers]]}'
kubectl delete pod web --[[force]] --[[grace-period]]=0
items.why: The API server will not remove an object while a finalizer is listed; force with grace-period 0 drops it from etcd without waiting for the kubelet.

items.title: Default-deny NetworkPolicy
items.text:
apiVersion: [[networking.k8s.io/v1]]
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: default-deny
  namespace: prod
spec:
  [[podSelector]]: {}
  [[policyTypes]]: [Ingress, Egress]
items.why: An empty podSelector selects every Pod in the namespace; naming a policyType with no matching rules denies that direction.

items.title: Allow one app on one port
items.text:
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels: { app: db }
  policyTypes: [Ingress]
  [[ingress]]:
    - [[from]]:
        - podSelector:
            matchLabels: { app: web }
      [[ports]]:
        - protocol: TCP
          port: 5432
items.why: Entries in the from list are separate peers (OR); selectors under a single dash must all match the same peer (AND).

items.title: Expose and pin a NodePort
items.text:
kubectl expose deploy web --port=80 --[[target-port]]=8080 --type=[[NodePort]]
kubectl create service nodeport web --tcp=80:8080 --[[node-port]]=[[30080]]
items.why: --port is what the Service listens on, --target-port is the container's port. NodePorts must fall in 30000-32767.

items.title: Imperative Ingress
items.text:
kubectl create ingress web \
  --[[rule]]="app.example.com/*=web:80" \
  --[[class]]=nginx -n prod
items.why: The rule syntax is host/path=service:port; a * suffix means pathType Prefix, and without it Exact.

items.title: HTTPRoute attaches to a Gateway
items.text:
apiVersion: [[gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1]]
kind: HTTPRoute
metadata: { name: web, namespace: prod }
spec:
  [[parentRefs]]:
    - name: prod-gw
      namespace: infra
  hostnames: ["app.example.com"]
  rules:
    - matches:
        - path: { type: [[PathPrefix]], value: /api }
      [[backendRefs]]:
        - name: api-svc
          port: 8080
items.why: parentRefs is what binds a route to a Gateway; whether the Gateway accepted it shows up in status.parents[].conditions.

items.title: Headless Service
items.text: kubectl create service clusterip db --[[clusterip]]="[[None]]"
items.why: clusterIP: None makes DNS return Pod IPs instead of a virtual IP — how StatefulSet members become individually addressable.

items.title: Rollout control
items.text:
kubectl [[set image]] deploy/web nginx=nginx:1.27
kubectl rollout [[status]] deploy/web
kubectl rollout [[undo]] deploy/web --[[to-revision]]=2
kubectl rollout [[restart]] deploy/web
items.why: set image patches one field and triggers exactly one rollout; rollout restart stamps the Pod template so a changed ConfigMap is picked up.

items.title: Zero-downtime strategy
items.text:
spec:
  strategy:
    type: RollingUpdate
    rollingUpdate:
      [[maxSurge]]: 1
      [[maxUnavailable]]: 0
items.why: maxUnavailable: 0 forces a new Pod to become Ready before an old one is removed.

items.title: HPA
items.text:
kubectl [[autoscale]] deploy web --min=2 --max=10 --[[cpu-percent]]=70
kubectl set [[resources]] deploy web --[[requests]]=cpu=100m
items.why: --cpu-percent is a percentage of the container's CPU request, so with no request the HPA reports <unknown> forever.

items.title: Taints
items.text:
kubectl taint nodes worker-1 gpu=true:[[NoExecute]]      # evicts running Pods too
kubectl taint nodes worker-1 gpu=true:NoSchedule[[-]]     # remove
kubectl get nodes -o [[custom-columns]]=NAME:.metadata.name,TAINTS:.spec.taints
items.why: NoExecute is the only effect that evicts already-running Pods; a trailing dash means remove.

items.title: ConfigMap and Secret creation
items.text:
kubectl create configmap app-cfg --[[from-literal]]=LOG_LEVEL=debug
kubectl create configmap app-cfg --[[from-env-file]]=./app.env   # one key per line
kubectl create secret [[generic]] db --from-literal=password=s3cr3t
kubectl get secret db -o [[jsonpath]]='{.data.password}' | [[base64]] -d
items.why: --from-file gives one key holding the whole file; --from-env-file gives one key per KEY=value line. Secret values are base64, not encrypted.

items.title: Static PV
items.text:
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolume
metadata: { name: pv-data }
spec:
  [[capacity]]:
    storage: 2Gi
  [[accessModes]]:
    - [[ReadWriteOnce]]
  [[persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy]]: Retain
  [[storageClassName]]: manual
  hostPath:
    path: /mnt/data
items.why: A PV binds only when capacity >= request, accessModes are a superset, and storageClassName matches exactly.

items.title: StorageClass
items.text:
apiVersion: [[storage.k8s.io/v1]]
kind: StorageClass
metadata:
  name: fast
  annotations:
    [[storageclass.kubernetes.io/is-default-class]]: "true"
provisioner: ebs.csi.aws.com
[[volumeBindingMode]]: WaitForFirstConsumer
[[reclaimPolicy]]: Delete
[[allowVolumeExpansion]]: true
items.why: WaitForFirstConsumer delays volume creation until a node is chosen, avoiding a volume stranded in the wrong zone; expansion is impossible without allowVolumeExpansion.

items.title: Reuse a Retained PV
items.text:
kubectl patch pv pv-data -p '{"spec":{"[[claimRef]]": null}}'
kubectl patch pv pv-data -p '{"spec":{"[[persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy]]":"Retain"}}'
items.why: A Released PV still points at its old claim; clearing claimRef returns it to Available.

items.title: Mount a PVC
items.text:
spec:
  containers:
    - name: app
      image: nginx
      [[volumeMounts]]:
        - name: data
          [[mountPath]]: /usr/share/nginx/html
  [[volumes]]:
    - name: data
      [[persistentVolumeClaim]]:
        [[claimName]]: pvc-data
items.why: The volume name is the join between volumes and volumeMounts — a mismatch there is the most common silent failure.

items.title: Exam shell setup
items.text:
alias k=kubectl
source <(kubectl [[completion]] bash)
export do='--[[dry-run]]=client -o yaml'
export now='--force --[[grace-period]]=0'
# ~/.vimrc
set [[expandtab]] tabstop=2 shiftwidth=2
items.why: $do turns every create/run into a manifest generator, and expandtab prevents literal tabs, which YAML rejects outright.
